title.narrative: Provide integrated nutrition services to most vulnerable communities in under-served and hard-to-reach rural areas in Buale district.

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to IPC findings released in March 2025 show an increase in the number of people projected to face acute levels of hunger in Somalia. An estimated 4.6 million people will remain acutely food insecure between April and June 2025, while 1.8 million children will continue to be acutely malnourished, 479,000 of them with severe acute malnutrition until the end of the year. Compared to the same season last year, the current estimate represents a 4% increase in Global Acute Malnutrition and a 9% increase in Severe Acute Malnutrition. The key drivers of acute food insecurity include poor rainfall, flooding, conflict and insecurity, high food prices, diseases and poor access to health services. The worsening of acute malnutrition is driven by the closure of health facilities, suspension of therapeutic and supplementary feeding programmes due to the cumulative effect of access to humanitarian assistance in Buale district.ltbrgtHowever, this project will cover curative and preventative interventions targeting children under 5 and pregnant and lactating women. Both active and passive screening for malnutrition will be conducted primarily at the community level through CHWs and Mother-led MUAC screening and at the health facilities level by nutrition staff. Mother-led mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) screening approach will be used, where mothers are trained to screen for acute malnutrition in their children by measuring MUAC and testing for edema. Malnourished women and children will be admitted to the relevant OTP or TSFP programs. Complicated cases of SAM will be referred to the stabilization center in Buale health facility. According to MoH guidelines, children and pregnant and lactating women will receive relevant micronutrient supplementation such as iron/folate, Micronutrient powder and tablets deworming and Vitamin A. SORDES will ensure active Community-level mobilization and education, identification of malnourished cases, mass campaigns and follow-ups at homes through nutrition volunteers and outreach/mobile teams would be the hallmark for universal coverage. SORDES will ensure inclusion of minorities and disable group as well as these far hard to reach areas in Buale hence ensuring improved referral and strengthen services utilization among the vulnerable group in Buale district, SORDES shall also endeavor to conduct caregiver’s infant and young child feeding practices, IYCF promotion session for better information dissemination to the caregivers in the project area to ensure proper services delivery at Qodaxley,Horseed, Reebay, Baqdaad,Waberi, Heegan and Halgan mobile nutrition sites and Bula town static nutrition facility will be provided to the hard-to-reach areas. SORDES with its technical team will integrate surveillance and emergency preparedness in the program so that enough steps are taken in ensuring early response to both nutrition cases and this will be coordinated with the local actors in the regionltbrgtlt/pgt
